stories.headline: Trump rejects Iran’s proposed roadmap to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz

sources.body:
Only a "negotiated solution" can end the conflict between the US and Iran, Tehran's foreign minister has said, after President Donald Trump publicly rejected a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump told reporters at the White House that Iran's proposal was not "acceptable" and that Tehran wanted to make a deal to open the strait to commercial shipping within seven days because "they're losing so badly".

In a post on Telegram, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi acknowledged Trump's rejection, but said Iran would wait for a "definitive" official US response.

He said the president had made contradictory statements in the past.

Araghchi said the conditions to open the strait were the same that had been included in a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the US and Iran that was signed in June.

Iran said it had raised reopening the strait and ending hostilities during negotiations on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this past week.

The vital waterway through which around a fifth of the world's gas and oil supply usually flows has been effectively closed since the outbreak of war in February.

"I'm rejecting their deal," Trump said on Saturday, adding that the US already had "total control" of the strait, with "massive amounts of oil" passing through it, causing massive rises in global oil prices and steep fuel cost increases for consumers.

Araghchi wrote on Telegram that Trump "has made many good statements, as well as many contradictory ones, which unfortunately we hear frequently".

He continued: "We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive views to us, and we will make a decision based on them."

Separately, Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, who travelled to New York for the UN general assembly , told the BBC's US news partner CBS that "distrust created by this war needs to be overcome" in order for talks to be successful.

He said the Iranians were open to talks on implementing the MOU in stages in order to end the impasse, but that the "US needs to show it does not intend to overthrow our government".

Pezeshkian said Trump had "tore up" the MOU when the US resumed its bombing campaign, adding: "If we don't abide by what we have written down, can we really resolve it by dialogue?"

He was also asked about Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who was injured in the US strike which killed his father in February and has not been seen in public since. Reports have claimed he suffered serious injuries to his legs and face.

Pezeshkian said he had met the supreme leader on two occasions, telling CBS he had "no specific ongoing health issues or challenges" and had been well enough to hold seven hours of talks.

Oman, which has been acting as a mediator between the US and Iran, called for all parties to continue having open dialogue to resolve the crisis.

Oman's foreign minister, Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Albusaidi, told the UN General Debate that "all parties" should cooperate with Oman in efforts to safeguard navigation in the strategic waterway.
sources.headline: Iranian minister says only negotiation can end conflict after Trump rejects Hormuz deal

sources.body:
Iran’s seven-day timetable would restart nuclear talks, but will the US be willing to deliver on terms that include reining in Israel in Lebanon?

Iran’s seven-day timetable to reopen the strait of Hormuz and start talks on its nuclear programme has been pitched as a deal that could rapidly extricate Donald Trump from a political crisis but requires the US president to make difficult concessions.

In the five days left before the proposed reopening of the strait, which is expected to relieve pressure on global energy markets, Trump would need to lift Iranian asset freezes, permit Iran to export its oil and, probably most difficult of all, order Benjamin Netanyahu to end Israel’s attacks on Hezbollah in Lebanon , thus achieving the “ceasefire on all fronts”.

Iranian diplomats in New York said they thought a three-hour meeting earlier this week with the US envoy Steve Witkoff in which they laid out the seven-day plan was productive, but were doubtful the US would deliver.

Iran nevertheless feels it has done the diplomatic spadework, taking the proposal to China for endorsement and ensuring that Oman, located on the south side of the strait, was also on board.

The foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, explained that the idea was to take the elements of the Iran-US memorandum of understanding that Trump signed in June and repackage and accelerate the process since, as they understood it, Trump had come to hate the MoU.

“The conditions we have asked the US to meet is nothing new, nothing more than what was already in the Islamabad agreement, which was signed by the US president,” Araghchi said. But what is new is the speed.

In the first four to five days under this timetable, the US would have to lift the naval blockade on Iran’s oil ports, restore the waiver that lifted sanctions on Iran’s oil exports, end the war on all fronts and permit the release of some of Iran’s frozen assets.

On the sixth day, the strait of Hormuz would be reopened by Iran, with ships using a new route designated by Oman and Iran. And on the next day, negotiations would start on the future of Iran’s civil nuclear programme, including a protocol to allow UN nuclear inspectors back in to look at Iran’s damaged sites and the stockpile of highly enriched uranium. This accelerates the point at which nuclear talks would begin, from 60 days in the June agreement to seven.

Those talks could, of course, take a long time, but from Trump’s perspective, the strait of Hormuz would be reopened before the midterm elections, a point in the political calendar that the Iranian president, Masoud Pezeshkian, says has never been a factor in Iranian thinking. Trump had claimed Iran was waiting until after the vote to offer a deal.

Iran, Araghchi argued at a largely off-the-record briefing with reporters – at which Pezeshkian was also present – had every reason not to negotiate with the US.

In particular, he admitted to being sceptical that Witkoff could deliver. He recounted how he had twice held talks with Trump’s special envoy, after which Witkoff had described them as “productive and good”, only for the US to bomb Iran the next day. Other Iranian diplomats say Trump’s willingness to rein in Netanyahu in Lebanon remains key. If he could do that, a deal would be feasible.
sources.headline: Trump faces tough choices as Iran dangles deal to reopen Hormuz before US midterms

sources.body:
Tehran says it is awaiting an official response through mediators and that it will not back down from its conditions.

Araghchi ignores Trump, waits for mediators’ response on Hormuz

United States President Donald Trump has rejected a plan submitted by Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, as Tehran continued to insist that only diplomacy can solve the conflict between the two countries.

Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said on Saturday that Iran wants to make a deal to open the vital maritime corridor immediately only “because they are losing so badly”.

“They want to make a deal, and I think that’s fine. I’d like to make a deal, too,” he said. But the proposal put forth by Iran “would not be acceptable,” he said.

The plan by Iran, announced on Friday at the United Nations General Assembly, calls for the US to release frozen Iranian funds, lift oil sanctions and end its naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s foreign minister, said at the time that those steps could be completed within four or five days, clearing the way for the strait to reopen and for negotiations on a final agreement to begin by the seventh day.

Araghchi responded to Trump’s rejection in a post on his Telegram channel on Saturday, saying Iran “will not back down” on its conditions.

“We have seen the first reaction from the US president, but nothing has been conveyed to us from the mediators yet,” Araghchi wrote, adding that Trump had a history of making “contradictory” statements.

He said Iran was “waiting for the definitive opinions to be conveyed to us by the mediators” and would “make a decision based on that”. He added that “only a negotiated solution” can get the US “out of this deadlock”.

US officials had signalled on Friday that Trump would reject the proposal. The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed US officials, reported that Trump was “privately sceptical” that Tehran would meet his demands. He reportedly told aides that he expects a renewed bombing campaign on Iran after the US midterm elections in November.

Al Jazeera’s Mike Hanna, reporting from Washington, DC, said the Iranian proposal appears “dead in the water”. But he noted Trump has offered no alternative.

“The one thing that has been made clear by President Trump is that he is content to stay in the status of limbo,” Hanna said, “despite concerns from much of the American public that the Iran conflict is turning into another ‘never-ending war’.”

Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway critical to global oil supplies, shortly after the US and Israel launched their war on February 28. Iranian attacks on vessels in the waterway have since sharply curtailed shipping.

The US has responded with an economic blockade on Iran and threats of secondary sanctions against airports and companies doing business with Iranian airlines – measures that have already prompted the United Arab Emirates, Iraq and Oman to cancel flights .

Earlier in the week, Araghchi met with Steve Witkoff, Trump’s envoy, to lay out conditions for ending the war, which would also include waiving oil sanctions and establishing a regional ceasefire covering Lebanon and Yemen.

stories.headline: UK police arrest men and evacuate homes near RAF Fairford over suspected explosives offences

sources.body:
A major incident has been declared and homes have been evacuated in a village near an RAF base which hosts the United States Air Force.

Several men have been arrested on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act, Gloucestershire police said. An army explosive ordnance disposal team is currently examining a number of vehicles.

Residents in Whelford, near RAF Fairford, have been taken to a leisure centre while investigations continue, police said. A cordon is currently in place in the area and officers say they believe the incident is contained.

The base has been recently used to deploy American bombers since the country's conflict in Iran began on 28 February.

In March this year, after then prime minister Sir Keir Starmer granted permission for "defensive" US action against Iranian missile sites from UK bases, four American bombers landed at RAF Fairford and the US started using British bases for "specific defensive operations".

A large emergency services presence has been seen in the area, including a Hazardous Area Response Team.

Gloucestershire Police said: "A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident.

"It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act.

"We are working closely with our partners and are enacting the well-rehearsed plans we have in place."

Police said the men were arrested early on Sunday morning.

A spokesperson for the US Air Force said its personnel based at RAF Fairford "remain vigilant".

They said: "For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures.

"The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families.

"We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families."

sources.headline: Men held in major incident near RAF Fairford as homes evacuated

sources.body:
Police say they have arrested several men on suspicion of explosives-related offences and bomb disposal experts are examining vehicles.

Police have evacuated homes near an airbase in the United Kingdom used by the United States military and arrested several men on suspicion of explosives-related offences.

“The army’s specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently ⁠examining a number of vehicles,” Gloucestershire police said on Sunday, adding that “a major incident” had been declared.

Residents from a number of properties in Whelford, southwestern England, were being taken to a nearby leisure centre. Police said several men had been arrested “on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act”.

The town is located near RAF Fairford, an airbase that US forces have used for strikes during the US-Israel war on Iran.

A reporter from the Reuters news agency at the scene said armed police had blocked access to the base’s main gate, while equipment had been placed in front of entry points.

About 30 emergency vehicles, including police cars, ambulances and fire engines, were stationed in the nearby town of Fairford.

Gloucestershire police said in a statement they would like “to reassure people that we believe this incident is contained”.

There was no immediate information about what prompted the arrests, whether explosives were found, or if the suspected offences were connected to the airbase.

The US Air Force said it was aware of reports about the incident but declined to discuss specific security measures.

A spokesperson said the 501st Combat Support Wing, a US Air Force unit in Britain, and other US units based in the UK remained vigilant and would take steps needed to protect personnel and their families.

In March, three US B-1B Lancer bombers touched down at RAF Fairford after what is believed to be the first US strike mission against Iran launched from a British base, during the war on Iran.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a powerful military force that operates alongside the country’s regular armed forces, warned in July that bases used to launch attacks on Iran could be treated as legitimate targets.

Authorities have not linked Sunday’s arrests to Iran or said RAF Fairford was a target.

stories.headline: Two mass shootings in South African townships kill at least 27 people

sources.body:
Twenty-seven people have been killed in two mass shootings hours apart in South Africa, the latest gun violence to hit the country.

Seventeen people were killed when eight gunmen stormed a bar close to Johannesburg on Saturday evening, with 15 more injured.

In a separate shooting in the early hours of Sunday morning, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town and a further 11 were injured.

South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world and has struggled to contain gang-related gun violence in recent years. Police have not indicated a motive for either of the latest attacks.

In Johannesburg, gunmen opened fire on customers outside the bar before continuing the attack inside and torching two vehicles before fleeing.

Police said thirteen men and four women were killed.

Deputy provincial police commissioner Maj Gen Fred Kekana said the attack may have been a retaliation for an incident last month, in which one person was killed and another wounded, according to AFP news agency.

Speaking at the scene, he said police had clear pictures and in some cases names for the suspects.

In Cape Town, five victims died at the scene and a further five people died in hospital.

No arrests had been made in either case on Sunday morning.

The two mass shootings came days after 11 people were killed in the city of Durban when gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township.

Illegal weapons are prevalent in South Africa and gun violence has been a persistent problem for decades, with about 60 murders recorded every day in the country of 62 million.

But a recent spate of mass shootings has raised fears that the problem is deepening, with violence often linked to turf wars between gangs engaged in drug trafficking and illegal mining.

In February, President Cyril Ramaphosa called organised crime "the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development".

Earlier this year the military was deployed alongside police in areas with the highest murder rates in an effort to reduce armed violence.

On Saturday a tenth woman's body was found in Ekurhuleni , to the east of Johannesburg, with local police saying they were unable to rule out a serial killer operating in the area with similarities between the deaths.
sources.headline: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead

sources.body:
Seventeen people killed at bar near Johannesburg and 10 killed in separate incident at barbecue venue near Cape Town

Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, police have said.

The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, south-west of Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.

In a separate statement, police said 10 people had been killed in a mass shooting at an entertainment venue selling grilled meat, known as a shisanyama , in Lwandle, near Cape Town. Another 11 people were wounded in that shooting. Police said they were searching for multiple suspects, without giving an exact number.

The two attacks happened days after a mass shooting by three gunmen at a house party near the east coast city of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.

No arrests had been made in the two latest mass shootings, police said.

South Africa has struggled with high rates of violent crime for years, but the series of mass shootings this week were shocking even to a country used to some of the highest violent crime rates in the world.

Police in the province of Gauteng said on Sunday morning they had launched a manhunt for the unidentified eight suspects in the Johannesburg tavern shooting, with no arrests yet made.

“It is alleged that patrons were drinking inside and outside the tavern when the suspects arrived and opened fire on those outside,” a police spokesperson, Capt Tintswalo Sibeko, said in a statement.

“The suspects then entered the tavern and continued shooting at patrons inside. The suspects were reportedly armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols. They allegedly searched some patrons and took their cellphones before fleeing the scene in two unidentified motor vehicles. Two vehicles were also set alight during the incident.”

Western Cape police said they had set up a team led by serious violent crime detectives to investigate the Cape Town shooting, in which the gunmen entered the shinsanyama venue at about 1.46am on Saturday night and starting shooting at customers.

“Five individuals died on the scene while five others succumbed to injuries sustained after being transported to medical facilities,” the statement said. “Eleven others are receiving medical treatment for injuries sustained … Detectives are hard at work in search of the perpetrators of the shooting incident with no arrests effected yet. The identities of the deceased persons will be released once their next of kin are informed.”

In the 12 months to 30 June, more than 22,700 people were murdered in South Africa, according to police data .

South Africans are already reeling after the discovery of numerous women’s bodies near Johannesburg’s airport since July, most of which were found in the last few weeks. The killings led to renewed anger about high rates of gender-based violence in the country and has piled pressure on police and politicians to do more about it.
sources.headline: At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say

sources.body:
Incidents in Wedela southwest of ​Johannesburg and Lwandle near Cape Town come days after Durban mass shooting.

At least 27 people have been killed and more than 20 wounded in two shootings in two South African townships, according to police.

In the first incident late on Saturday, at least 17 people were killed and 15 wounded in a shooting at a tavern in Wedela southwest of Johannesburg.

Police said they were searching for eight suspects, who were “reportedly armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols”. The motive for the shooting remained unknown, and no arrests were announced.

Early on Sunday, gunmen killed at least 10 people and wounded 11 at a store in Lwandle near Cape Town.

The shootings took place just days after a shooting at a house party near the city of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.

In the first incident, police said the attack began about 9:30pm (19:30 GMT) on Saturday in Extension 3, Wedela, in Gauteng province’s West Rand district.

The gunmen fired at people gathered outside the tavern before going inside, where more shots were fired. Investigators said some customers were searched during the attack and had their mobile phones taken.

The suspects then escaped in two vehicles. Two other vehicles were burned during the incident.

Captain Tintswalo Sibeko said detectives and specialist police units had been assigned to identify and find the eight suspects, with police opening 17 murder cases and 15 attempted murder cases as well as two cases related to property damage.

In the second incident, police said they were searching for multiple suspects after the shooting that took place after midnight on Sunday.

South Africa records persistently high levels of violent crime, including killings involving firearms.

The government has faced sustained pressure to improve public safety, particularly in major urban areas where police have carried out additional operations against gun crimes.
sources.headline: At least 27 people killed in two shootings in South African townships

stories.headline: Powerful nor’easter brings flooding and emergency declarations in New York and New Jersey

sources.body:
Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm bringing coastal flooding, power cuts, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events.

The so-called nor'easter is bringing "dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston on Saturday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said.

States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, both of which faced a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds are forecast from Virginia to Maine.

In Brooklyn, a man was killed by a falling tree, the BBC's US partner CBS News reported.

The nor'easter has caused widespread power cuts. More than 100,000 households, nearly all in the northeast US, have lost electricity, according to tracker PowerOutage.

The Federal Aviation Administration recommended air passengers check with airlines about their flight status. More than 2,400 flights have been delayed and another 1,199 grounded, according to FlightAware.

Saturday's full moon is projected to worsen coastal flooding. Streets and homes were inundated with floodwater in the coastal New Jersey communities of Surf City and Manasquan on Saturday.

"I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert and follow local guidance," Governor Mikie Sherrill said.

NWS said in its alert: "Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses."

In New York, officials are warning of wind gusts of up to 55mph (86km/h) throughout the weekend, leading to downed trees and power lines.

"Don't travel if you don't have to," NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents in a video message. "Do not drive or walk through floodwater."

In the Boston area, the Red Sox moved the last game in their series against the Chicago Cubs to Sunday afternoon in Florida.

A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled.

The Global Citizen Festival concert in New York City's Central Park, which was to be headlined by Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend, will not go ahead.

Ed Sheeran's Boston concert was also among events called off due to the weather.

Sheeran's concert at the Gillette Stadium in the Boston area was cancelled for safety reasons, the venue said.
sources.headline: Nor'easter brings flooding as New York and New Jersey declare emergency

stories.headline: Poll finds Trump’s MAGA base less concerned about affordability than other voters

sources.body: Not everyone thinks there’s an affordability crisis. While many Americans say the cost of living is the top issue facing the U.S. more than any other, President Donald Trump’s MAGA base does not always agree, according to a new analysis of The POLITICO Poll . Just 28 percent of voters who self-identify as part of the MAGA movement say expenses have become less affordable since Trump took office. In fact, MAGA voters are more likely to say things have gotten better rather than worse. That’s a stark break from the rest of the country, including the voters who backed Kamala Harris in 2024 and those who voted for Trump but do not identify as part of the MAGA movement. The POLITICO Poll results reveal a complicated challenge for Republicans: In an election all about the economy, cost of living concerns are reinforcing partisanship divides — entrenching Democrats’ opposition to Trump — while also driving a wedge among Republicans’ own base. Now, GOP candidates are facing frustrated voters from all sides. Harris voters are far more likely than Trump voters to say groceries, gas and other expenses have gotten more expensive since the president took office, despite facing similar increases in household costs, according to a POLITICO analysis of cost of living data. Democrats hope to ride that frustration to victory in November, and have made affordability their top messaging issue this fall. They’re poised to benefit from the backlash to Trump’s economic agenda — from his unpopular tariffs to an Iran war that’s raised gas prices — which politicians and strategists widely agree are helping motivate Democratic voters. “Those Democrats are definitely going to go vote,” said Michigan-based GOP strategist Jason Roe. “And we've got some voters that are a little harder to get to the polls, and when they are mad, frustrated, disappointed, disillusioned, in disagreement, and we don't have them motivated, that's going to be a problem.” Many of those disillusioned Trump voters, The POLITICO Poll suggests, are the ones who don’t identify as part of the MAGA base. Consider the 52% of non-MAGA Trump voters who say the cost of living in their area is the “worst” it has ever been: Nearly half say they either wouldn’t vote for a Republican in the midterms or are still making up their minds. But what is a boon to Democrats today could be a problem for them later. Partisanship also shapes how Americans remember the economy in years past, the poll results show. Harris voters have a more favorable memory toward Democratic presidents and Trump voters have a more favorable memory toward Republican presidents, each saying life was more affordable when their party held the reins. Democrats and Republicans simply don’t share an understanding of the economic reality — and without a common frame for the past, nor whether things are improving in the present, any party in power stands to lose its grip against an increasingly frustrated opposition when the economy is the key issue. This year, that will be a major challenge for Republicans. MAGA vs. Non-MAGA vs. Democrats The POLITICO Poll asked adults across America last month about affordability in their area, including about local prices and their memory of when prices were more affordable in the past. Across the board, Harris voters outpaced Trump voters in their pessimism about the economy. And among Trump voters, non-MAGA voters outpaced their MAGA counterparts. For example, 70% of Harris voters and 52% of non-MAGA Trump voters say the cost of living is worse than they can “ever remember it being.” MAGA Trump voters disagreed — a 43% plurality said the cost of living today is bad, but they could “remember times when it was worse.” The results are a warning sign about the Trump coalition: In question after question, the president’s most loyal base is still sticking with him, but among the non-MAGA voters he convinced to back him in 2024, their frustration more closely resembles how Harris voters feel. "There will be voters who voted for Donald Trump in 2024 who know he's made life more expensive and won't vote for his party this time," said longtime Democratic strategist Jesse Ferguson. "Some will vote for a Democrat, some won't vote. But they won't cast a ballot for a Republican who they blame for the high cost of living." Of the non-MAGA Trump voters who say the cost of living is the worst they’ve seen, just 53% say they would vote for a Republican if the midterms were held tomorrow. More than 25% would vote for a Democrat or third-party candidate. The rest say they would stay home or have not yet made up their minds. Changes to family budgets are similar on average among those that voted for Trump and those who voted for Harris, according to a POLITICO analysis of data from the Living Wage Institute, a nonpartisan public benefit corporation that produces cost of living data. Across the country, family budgets have increased by 2.5 percent on average from early 2025 to early 2026, according to the Living Wage Institute. But it is the concept of who is to blame that creates division among each voting bloc. Though each group is concerned about affordability — the cost of living is the most common concern for each — only MAGA Trump voters remain sympathetic to the current administration. Young voters — and young men in particular — have also grown disillusioned with the Trump administration amid cost of living concerns, a warning sign for the GOP. Among those under the age of 25 who say the cost of living is the worst it’s ever been, 56% say they trust Democrats to bring down the costs. Just 20% trust Republicans to do the same. “Young people feel like the system isn't working for them,” said Joe Mitchell, a Republican running for Iowa’s open and competitive 2nd District. Mitchell, who is 29, would be the second Gen Z member to join the House if elected. “You see them being attracted to some of these DSA candidates like Zohran Mamdani. And they're going to be attracted to these candidates if we don't figure something out for them now.” Partisanship even drives memory Partisanship also colors how Americans see the past, making it difficult for any incumbent party to convince voters of plans for the future. The POLITICO Poll asked respondents whether it was easier or harder to afford everyday items in years past compared to today in one of two ways: In one, they were asked about a specific calendar year, and in another, the presidential administration in power at the time. For each question framed around a calendar year, Trump and Harris voters gave similar answers. But when asked to compare how easy or hard it was to afford things during a particular presidential administration compared to today, their answers split along party lines. For example, just over a third of both Harris and Trump voters said it was “easier” to afford everyday items in 2024 compared to today. But when asked the same question about the “end of [former President] Joe Biden’s term,” 55% of Harris voters said everyday items were easier to afford, compared to 39% of Trump voters. The results show that Americans lack a common frame of reference on the issue most people care about — the cost of living — creating a massive hurdle for politicians hoping to win over new voters who may not be willing to listen. The same effect happens among Trump voters looking back on a Democratic administration. When asked about costs in 2010 compared to today, 63% of Trump voters said everyday items were easier to afford then compared to now. But when asked about costs during the “middle” of former President Barack Obama’s first term — or 2010 — only 36% of Trump voters said the same. It’s only when a political party is attached that Americans’ version of the truth changes. When POLITICO asked whether it was easier or harder to afford everyday items “just before the Covid-19 pandemic” or in “2019,” majorities from both parties said things were easier to afford then, and in both framings. The challenge for both parties is that voters don’t know “who has a better plan for the future,” GOP communications strategist Kevin Madden said. “Instead, what you’re seeing is a gap — or a canyon — emerge between the rest of the country and Washington.” He added: “When you see that gap emerge, watch out if you’re an incumbent.” Alisa Vasquez and Andrew Howard contributed to this report.
sources.headline: Poll: Trump’s MAGA loyalists don’t think he has an affordability problem

sources.body:
Centenares de personas ha acampado desde la pasada madrugada de este domingo en la madrileña Puerta del Sol como protesta por la crisis de la vivienda, exclamando que no aguantan más y que "o cae el rentismo o cae el Gobierno". La acampada se ha iniciado a primeras horas de la noche del sábado, al término de la manifestación que se celebró en el centro de Madrid para protestar por el desahucio de Maricarmen, la anciana que tuvo que abandonar su casa de alquiler tras 70 años en la misma, y reclamar medidas efectivas para frenar la crisis de la vivienda.

En un clima de tranquilidad y sin incidencias reportadas, los congregados han pasado la noche en alrededor de un centenar de tiendas de campaña que han ido instalando con el paso de las horas, siguiendo el llamamiento hecho por el Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos de Madrid, impulsor de la iniciativa.

La portavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas, Alicia del Río, ha explicado en una entrevista en el Canal 24 Horas que si no se aprueban las medidas del 'decreto Maricarmen', el Gobierno no tiene sentido. "Tenemos claro que tenemos que ser muy contundentes. Habrá que seguir avanzando para que no le pase a nadie lo que le ha pasado a Maricarmen".

“ #Canal24Horas | Alicia del Río, portavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas, desde la acampada en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid: 🗣️ "Tenemos claro que tenemos que ser muy contundentes. Si no se aprueban las medidas del 'decreto Maricarmen', este Gobierno no tiene sentido [...] Habrá que… pic.twitter.com/1BWRCODhd4 “

El portavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas, Gonzalo Álvarez, es una de las persona que ha pasado la noche en Sol. "Estas horas han sido duras porque no es fácil pasar la noche al raso, pero se vive con ilusión, expectación y ganas de cambiarlo todo. Pedimos cambios estructurales y que la vivienda se trate como un bien de primera necesidad y no como un activo financiero", ha explicado en una entrevista en directo en el Canal 24. Exigen al Gobierno que el próximo martes aprueben un decreto que contemple, entre otros aspectos, la congelación de los precios de los alquileres. "Maricarmen ha prendido la chispa con la injusticia, la crudeza del caso y la actuación policial brutal", ha dicho.

El portavoz ha asegurado que de no aprobarse el próximo martes el decreto, los partidos de izquierda como Sumar deben hacer caer el Gobierno : "Se tiene que terminar. No tiene sentido que exista este supuesto".

“ #Canal24Horas | Gonzalo Álvarez, portavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas, desde la acampada en la Puerta del Sol: 🗣️"Qué pasa si el martes no se aprueba el decreto tal y como nosotras lo concebimos? Que este Gobierno se tiene que terminar. No tiene sentido que exista este supuesto… pic.twitter.com/Wdycae3gek “

"Hemos decidido acampar en Sol para exigir medidas reales en materia de vivienda. No aguantamos más este estado rentista que nos exprime y nos echa de nuestros barrios. Toda ayuda es bienvenida. Si no puedes venir a acampar, puedes traer sacos de dormir, esterillas, comida o agua", ha publicado en la red social X el Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos de Madrid.

Con la marioneta de un buitre con sombrero de copa presidiendo la Puerta del Sol de Madrid, varios cientos de manifestantes han pasado la noche acampados en protesta por la crisis de vivienda y exigiendo al Gobierno que el próximo martes apruebe en el Consejo de Ministros el que han llamado "decreto Maricarmen" , una norma que exigen que incluya los "alquileres indefinidos". Dispuestos a aumentar la presión sobre el Ejecutivo, desde primera hora de este domingo, rodeados por turistas y curiosos, los congregados en este 15-M de la Vivienda han empezado a organizarse para pasar, al menos, una noche más en el centro de la capital.

Talleres de resistencia pacífica, charlas sobre el mercado de la vivienda o una comida popular son algunas de las actividades programadas que se han colgado en un horario en el punto de bienvenida, una carpa naranja izada en mitad de la Puerta del Sol por el Sindicato de Inquilinas de Madrid . Algunos de los manifestantes, con cepillo y recogedor en mano, han empezado también a limpiar la zona de acampada, ante la atenta mirada de agentes de la Policía Nacional, cuyo número ha ido incrementándose con el paso de las horas.

"Hoy vamos a hacer noche también, igual que hicimos ayer. Mañana veremos cómo sigue todo", sostiene Gonzalo Álvare z, uno de los portavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas, que, además, apunta que la intención es celebrar a las 20:00 horas el 'Fuck Rent Fest'.

La intención de los acampados, explican, es presionar al Gobierno para que el martes se apruebe en el Consejo de Ministros el decreto con medidas para hacer frente a la crisis de la vivienda, el cual quieren que incluya la prórroga de los alquileres, el fin de los desahucios sin alternativa habitacional, la regulación de los alquileres por habitaciones y de temporada y la congelación de los precios del alquiler.

"Si no se cumplen estas medidas, el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez y la ministra de Vivienda Isabel Rodríguez tiene que romperse, no tiene ningún sentido -asevera Álvarez-. Llevamos ocho años de supuesto gobierno progresista, ¿dónde está el Gobierno progresista, dónde está la Legislatura de la vivienda? Es un sin sentido, no han conseguido hacer nada y si no son capaces de plegarse a nuestras exigencias tienen que romper el gobierno y los ministros de Sumar y todos los partidos a la izquierda del PSOE tienen que posicionarse, aclarar de qué lado están".

Igual de contundente ha sido la también portavoz del movimiento Alicia del Río. "Para que no haya ningún a Maricarmen más, contratos indefinidos, contratos, indefinidos y contratos indefinidos. No lo podemos explicar más claro. También se puede llamar renovación automática de los contratos, que no nos puedan echar, y si esto no se aprueba, rn este país siguen gobernando los fondos buitre", ha sentenciado ante el centenar de tiendas de campaña que se han instalado por toda la plaza.

sources.body: <p>Para ella llega tarde, porque su desahucio ya se ha ejecutado y se ha quedado sin casa. <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-25/maricarmen-desde-el-gregorio-maranon-gracias-a-todos-los-que-han-estado-conmigo-para-defender-mi-casa.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-25/maricarmen-desde-el-gregorio-maranon-gracias-a-todos-los-que-han-estado-conmigo-para-defender-mi-casa.html">Pero Maricarmen Abascal, a sus 87 años y </a>con una imagen de total fragilidad en su silla de ruedas, parece estar a punto de lograr un imposible: los grupos de la mayoría de investidura, que llevaban meses de batalla sin solución a la vista, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-24/el-gobierno-busca-apoyos-para-aprobar-el-martes-nuevas-medidas-contra-los-desahucios-como-el-de-maricarmen.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-24/el-gobierno-busca-apoyos-para-aprobar-el-martes-nuevas-medidas-contra-los-desahucios-como-el-de-maricarmen.html">parecen ahora forzados a encontrar un acuerdo </a>y dar un giro a la política de vivienda este martes con un decreto pactado entre todos. A la presión de la propia Maricarmen se sumó este sábado una manifestación masiva que interpeló sobre todo a Isabel Díaz Ayuso, presidenta de Madrid, a José Luis Martínez Almeida, alcalde de la ciudad, responsables de dar soluciones a la anciana, pero también a Pedro Sánchez y su Gobierno, exigiéndoles que este martes aprueben un decreto potente para impedir que haya más Maricarmenes. La presión es tan fuerte que es difícil pensar que se frustre esta vez el acuerdo, aunque tampoco es imposible porque las posiciones son contradictorias y hay vetos cruzados.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-27/maricarmen-fuerza-un-giro-del-gobierno-y-sus-socios-sobre-vivienda.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

sources.body: <p>A Maricarmen la han intentado desahuciar cuatro veces. La última, lo han conseguido. Hace cuatro días que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-25/maricarmen-desde-el-gregorio-maranon-gracias-a-todos-los-que-han-estado-conmigo-para-defender-mi-casa.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-25/maricarmen-desde-el-gregorio-maranon-gracias-a-todos-los-que-han-estado-conmigo-para-defender-mi-casa.html">duerme en una cama de hospital</a>, lejos de la que ha sido su casa durante siete décadas. La empresa Urbagestión compró su piso de Retiro (Madrid) en 2018 por un precio irrisorio para la zona precisamente porque ella vivía en él. Con una pensión de 1.400 euros, ella nunca ha dejado de pagar el alquiler, de renta antigua, y las facturas, unos 500 euros al mes en total. En 2020 los propietarios le dijeron que debía dejar el piso, porque el contrato ya había sido subrogado dos veces. Y desde entonces no han aceptado ninguna de las propuestas que han recibido —de la Administración, de particulares, de personalidades de la cultura— para o bien pagar la diferencia del alquiler (le pedían 1.600 euros) o comprar el apartamento. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-27/diseccion-del-desahucio-de-maricarmen-podria-haber-sido-diferente.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

sources.body:
El juez Juan Carlos Peinado , titular del Juzgado de Instrucción número 41 de Madrid, se jubila este domingo y lo hace después de dictar esta misma semana juicio oral con jurado popular contra Begoña Gómez , la mujer del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez , por los presuntos delitos de tráficos de influencias y malversación . También ha enviado a juicio a la asesora de Gómez, Cristina Álvarez, por malversación.

Peinado cuelga la toga el mismo día que cumple 72 años . En España, un juez se jubila de manera forzosa a los 70 años según la Ley Orgánica del Poder Judicial. Sin embargo, aquellos que lo soliciten con antelación pueden prolongar su permanencia en servicio hasta que se cumplan, como máximo, 72 años.

El magistrado pone fin de esta manera a una carrera profesional que ha estado marcada los últimos años por el procesamiento de la mujer del presidente del Gobierno; un caso que ha levantado críticas de 'lawfare' desde que arrancó en 2024 y que llevó al jefe del Ejecutivo a reflexionar sobre si dejaba la Presidencia .

Juan Carlos Peinado es licenciado en Derecho e ingresó a la carrera judicial cuando tenía 40 años por la vía del tercer turno , a través de un proceso de concurso-oposición y que exige contrar con un mínimo de años de ejercicio profesional. Desde 2016, Peinado es titular del Juzgado de Instrucción número 41 de Madrid. Antes pasó por juzgados de localidades de Ávila, Toledo y Albacete.

Además de las polémicas sobre la instrucción del caso de Begoña Gómez, la carrera de Peinado ha contado con varias polémicas. Una de ellas es cuando abrió una investigación contra Raúl González, exjugador del Real Madrid , por las gestiones de una de las empresas del futbolista.

Otro de los casos más destacados es la imputación de una docena de periodistas por revelación de secretos en el marco de la investigación policial en los Comités de Defensa de la República (CDR) en Cataluña durante el procés. El caso fue archivado finalmente en 2020.

La instrucción del caso Begoña Gómez ha sido uno de los últimos trabajos del juez Peinado. El magistrado ha puesto fin así a una investigación que arrancó hace casi dos años y medio a raíz de una denuncia del sindicato Manos Limpias y ahora será la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid la que fije la fecha de juicio, algo que se podría prolongar entre cuatro y ocho meses.

Durante todo este tiempo, el magistrado ha achacado y dejado de achacar a Gómez diferentes delitos, ha citado a declarar a ministros o al presidente del Gobierno y ha tenido que reconducir en alguna ocasión una instrucción que ha sido muy cuestionada .

Todo arrancó con una denuncia del pseudosindicato en abril de 2024 y que se basaba en recortes e informaciones publicadas en medios digitales, y de las cuales algunas eran inexactas, como reconoció el propio secretario general de Manos Limpias, que incluso llegó a decir que la denuncia podía contener noticias falsas . Tras ello, se sumaron a la causa la organización ultracatólica Hazte Oír o el partido Iusticia Europa.

stories.headline: Barcelona’s La Mercè festival concludes with its piromusical relocated to Nova Icària beach

sources.body:
Les festes de la Mercè acabaran els actes d'aquest any diumenge, 27 de setembre, amb el tradicional piromusical, que estrena nova ubicació.

El piromusical de la Mercè aquest any deixarà de celebrar-se a l'avinguda de Maria Cristina per les obres al recinte de la Fira de Montjuïc i es farà per primera vegada a la platja de la Nova Icària .

L'espectacle començarà a les 10 de la nit i durarà una mitja hora, amb foc i música sincronitzats. Es recomana desplaçar-se fins al passeig marítim en transport públic , que reforçarà les línies de bus i metro i augmentarà la capacitat i la freqüència de pas.

S'hi pot arribar amb metro per l' L4, Ciutadella | Vila Olímpica, i amb les línies d'autobús H16, V23, V25 i V27 . El metro funcionarà fins a la mitjanit.

Els aparcaments recomanats per als vehicles són BSM Marina Port o BSM Hospital del Mar.

Un any més, com en les últimes edicions, el piromusical de la Mercè 2026 encarrega a un artista la música que s'haurà d'acompanyar amb la pirotècnia. Un piromusical d'autor que vol posar en valor el talent local.

En aquesta ocasió, Josep Montero, líder i cantant d'Oques Grasses , és l'encarregat de seleccionar els temes que formaran part de la playlist de l'espectacle, amb una proposta eclèctica, oberta a diversos estils i sensibilitats , i amb una presència destacada de la música en català.

La mescla musical l'ha creat el dissenyador i tècnic de so Marçal Cruz , de l'estudi Oido, i la Pirotècnia Igual s'encarrega del disseny i la sincronització dels focs artificials amb la música de l'espectacle.

És el quart any en què un artista o grup convidat signa la banda sonora del piromusical. L'any passat se'n van encarregar els Estopa , mentre que l'any anterior va ser Rosalía qui va triar les cançons de l'espectacle de tancament de la Mercè.

La fórmula del piromusical de la Mercè d'autor es va estrenar el 2023 , quan se'n va encarregar el Sónar , coincidint amb el 30è aniversari d'aquest festival.

La participació d'Oques Grasses arriba pocs dies abans dels seus quatre concerts de comiat . Seran a l' Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys , entre el 5 i el 10 d'octubre, i sumaran uns 220.000 assistents en total.

El piromusical de la Mercè 2026, presentat per Dulceida, es podrà veure per TV3 i 3Cat .
sources.headline: El piromusical de la Mercè 2026, aquest diumenge a la platja de la Nova Icària: com arribar-hi

sources.body:
Com és tradicional, el piromusical tancarà les festes de la Mercè . Aquest any, però, la cita canvia d’escenari. Si fins ara s’havia celebrat a l’avinguda de Maria Cristina, a tocar de la plaça d’Espanya, enguany es trasllada a la platja de la Nova Icària . La raó són les obres que Fira de Barcelona executa a la mateixa avinguda. El piromusical és un dels esdeveniments més multitudinaris de la festa major de Barcelona.

L’espectacle tindrà lloc el darrer dia de la festa major, diumenge 27 de setembre, a les 22.00 hores. El fet que el nou escenari sigui una platja permetrà a la ciutadania veure els focs amb molta comoditat des de diferents punts del litoral de la capital catalana.

Des del 2023, l’Ajuntament encarrega la llista de cançons que sonaran durant el piromusical. Aquest any, la selecció l’ha triat Josep Montero , cantant d’ Oques Grasses . Els èxits que s’interpretaran no són peces del grup català, sinó temes de la història de la música elegits per Montero.

La banda d’Osona està a punt de retirar-se dels escenaris. Però ho farà per la porta gran, amb quatre concerts a l’Estadi Olímpic de Montjuïc els dies 5, 7, 9 i 10 d’octubre. Actuaran davant unes 220.000 persones. Les entrades estan esgotades des del novembre, quan es van posar a la venda.

Formada el 2010, Oques Grasses s’ha convertit en un fenomen molt rellevant de l’escena musical catalana dels darrers setze anys, amb una mescla de pop, reggae, funk, electrònica i sons urbans i molta personalitat sobre l’escenari.

Amb anterioritat a Oques Grasses, van elegir les cançons del piromusical el festival Sónar (l’any 2023, quan celebrava el 30è aniversari); Rosalia , el 2024, i Estopa , el 2025.

Per arribar fins a la platja de la Nova Icària, Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) reforçarà totes les línies de metro, però en especial l’L4, que és la que dona servei al litoral de la ciutat. Les estacions més properes són Ciutadella / Vila Olímpica i Barcelona. El metro funcionarà diumenge fins a mitjanit.

stories.headline: University pilot tests retractable solar pergolas to add shade to Barcelona’s heat-prone paved squares

sources.body: Les places dures van obrir-se pas a la ciutat en les dècades del 1980 i 1990. Van crear espais públics diàfans i es van executar de dues maneres diferents: o bé urbanitzant descampats o solars abandonats, o bé enderrocant edificis —procés conegut com a esponjament— per alliberar espai urbà . I en quasi tots els casos, es va aprofitar el solar per construir-hi, en el subsol , aparcaments o altres equipaments soterrats per aprofitar l’espai . Una fórmula que, a la superfície, feia inviable crear-hi zones verdes amb arbrat que proporcionessin ombra . També et pot interessar Menys espai per a “skates” i més verd i zones d’estada a la futura plaça dels Àngels Maria Solans 3 minuts de lectura Els arbres de les places dures Un dels grans efectes negatius d’aquestes places dures ha estat la calor . Han contribuït, i molt, a l’ efecte de l’illa de calor urbana i, alhora, han acabat espantant els ciutadans per utilitzar-les com un espai d’ús social habitual. Per revertir-ho, la UPC ha iniciat una prova pilot a la plaça del campus nord del centre universitari. Un espai dur i hostil perquè, arquitectònicament, és el sostre de les instal·lacions del servei d’esports universitari. Plaça del campus nord de la UPC, sense verd i sense zones d’ombra La prova consisteix en què, durant tot un any, dues pèrgoles —dissenyades pels estudiants d’enginyeria— oferiran ombra “a demanda” amb uns tendals retràctils en funció de l’època de l’any i que també podran generar energia mitjançant plaques solars . Alhora, totes dues pèrgoles preveuen espais d’estada i d’ús social a l’aixopluc de l’estructura. La idea es basa en un concepte molt simple: replicar la funció i les prestacions que ofereix un arbre de fulla caduca : guanya fullatge a la primavera i dona ombra en els mesos d’estiu , però el perd a la tardor per permetre que la radiació solar escalfi l’ambient a l’hivern . També et pot interessar Troba els arbres caducifolis al teu barri: prepara’t per viure els colors de la tardor Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo 2 minuts de lectura Capturador de contaminants Una de les propostes té una estructura de fusta —material que captura el CO 2 — amb un sostre que projecte ombra . Aquest sostre consta de plaques solars i una lona transpirable . Les plaques fotovoltaiques generen electricitat mentre reben la radiació solar, i és amb la lona on hi ha gran part de la novetat i l’enginy: deixa passar l’aire —i permet evacuar la calor del paviment de la plaça— i està feta amb un material catalític . Això vol dir que captura els elements contaminants que, en aquell moment, hi ha en l’ambient, tan bon punt hi entren en contacte. D’altra banda, el material de la lona catalítica és de color blanc i repel·leix la llum del sol i, per tant, evita que s’escalfi l’aire de la zona que queda aixoplugada a sota. Lona transpirable amb material catalític que, en ser de color blanc, repel·leix la llum solar La zona que queda sota de l’estructura que projecta l’ombra, s’ha dissenyat com un espai d’estada , amb bancs i taules per asseure’s-hi i petits parterres amb vegetació . L’estructura ha tingut la col·laboració de l’estudi d’enginyeria Esitec . Ombra a demanda L’altre projecte, amb estructura metàl·lica, té un tipus de disseny similar a l’anterior. Destaca per tenir uns panells que produeixen energia solar —opció fixa durant tot l’any— que combina amb un altres panells fets de làmines de fusta que projecten ombra i deixen passar l’aire —rebaixa la temperatura— però que a l’hivern es poden recollir per deixar entrar el sol i escalfar l’ambient per fer-lo més acollidor. Aquesta proposta també preveu la creació d’una zona d’estada amb mobiliari urbà , per tal d’usar-lo sota l’aixopluc de l’ombra. En aquest cas, el prototip neix d’una col·laboració a tres bandes : l’empresa de mobiliari urbà Benito ja tenia un prototip per crear ombra urbana —un pal amb una placa de làmines de fusta al capdamunt—, però mitjançant Eurecat , els estudiants d’enginyeria de la UPC l’han acabat evolucionat. L’estructura té panells solars i altres amb llàmines retràctils, per les diferents èpoques de l’any Si funciona, al carrer Els dos prototips són modulars , el que permet anar-los acoblant, un a un , per crear espais d’ombra més grans o més petits, en funció als carrers o les places on s’hagin d’instal·lar. Això serà un cop hagin superat la prova pilot , que durarà un any . Temps en què s’haurà d’ analitzar la temperatura i la humitat de dins i fora de la pèrgola —s’està mesurant amb uns sensors que hi ha instal·lats— per saber quanta frescor aporten a l’indret . També s’estudiarà el comportament de l’ estructura a la intempèrie —sota els efectes del sol, la calor extrema, les pluges i el vent— per saber la solidesa de les estructures i la fiabilitat dels materials usats, pel que fa als manteniments. D’altra banda, també s’haurà d’ analitzar l’ús social que els usuaris hagin fet de les zones d’estada dissenyades a l’interior de les pèrgoles , i les dinàmiques que s’hi hagin dut a terme, per determinar bé quins elements de mobiliari urbà hauran de tenir. Una vegada superada la prova pilot, doncs, els prototips estarien a punt perquè l’ Ajuntament pugui encarregar-ne la fabricació per instal·lar-los a la via pública. stories.headline: Summer sea temperatures off Girona break records, running 2.3°C above average

sources.body:
La Cala d'Aiguablava de Begur, en un imatge d'arxiu. / Istock

L’estiu del 2026 ha estat el més càlid des que hi ha registres oficials , segons el Meteocat. Seguint aquesta mateixa tendència, la temperatura de l’aigua del mar en superfície a les costes catalanes també ha trencat tots els rècords: 26,1 °C de mitjana , més de dos graus per sobre de la del període 1982-2022. De fet, tant juliol com agost s’anoten la temperatura mitjana més alta mai registrada, amb 27 °C i 28,4 °C en superfície , respectivament. I juny no bat el rècord, però per molt poc, i és el segon més càlid al mar, amb 23,7 °C de mitjana, des del 1982. Són dades de l’ Institut Català de Recerca per a la Governança del Mar (ICATMAR) , que també mostren temperatures màximes mensuals inèdites durant els tres mesos d’estiu. El balanç confirma, així, un episodi de calor marina excepcional tant per la intensitat dels valors assolits com per la seva persistència.

Segons els registres de temperatura màxima i mitjana d’ ICATMAR , elaborats a partir de dades del satèl·lit Copernicus, el litoral català s’ha escalfat aquest estiu molt per sobre de la mitjana climàtica, gairebé en consonància amb el que ha passat amb la temperatura ambiental. Si les estacions del Meteocat han registrat una anomalia de temperatura superior als 3 graus en bona part del país, al mar l’increment respecte de la mitjana de quaranta anys –1982-2022, de 23,8 °C– ha estat de 2,3 graus , una anomalia que no s’havia observat fins ara en tota la sèrie disponible.

Concretament, la temperatura mitjana durant el període juny-agost s’ha situat en els 26,1 graus centígrads . Mai, almenys des del 1982, s’havien superat els 26 °C de temperatura mitjana durant el conjunt dels tres mesos d’estiu, ni tan sols en el tòrrid estiu del 2022, que ostentava el rècord absolut fins ara amb 25,9 graus. El registre d’aquest 2026, per tant, supera una marca que ja s’havia situat en nivells excepcionalment elevats i consolida una nova referència en la sèrie climàtica del litoral català.

Dels tres mesos de l’estiu del 2026, el juny és l’únic que no ha assolit la temperatura mitjana mensual més alta de la sèrie, amb 23,7 graus, i queda en segon lloc només per darrere del juny de l’any passat, quan la temperatura mitjana va arribar als 24,1 °C. Malgrat això, el registre continua sent extraordinàriament elevat i confirma que l’ escalfament del mar ja es va fer evident des de l’inici de l’estiu. La temperatura elevada de l’aigua, per tant, no va ser un fenomen concentrat únicament en les setmanes centrals de juliol i agost.

Al juliol es va arribar per primera vegada als 27 graus de temperatura mitjana , una xifra que no tenia precedents en els registres disponibles. I l’agost també fa miques tots els registres amb 28,42 graus de temperatura mitjana , gairebé 3 per sobre de la mitjana del conjunt dels mesos d’agost del període 1982-2022 i mig grau per sobre del darrer rècord, assolit el 2022. És, amb diferència, el mes més excepcional dels tres que formen l’estiu meteorològic i el que més clarament evidencia la magnitud de l’episodi d’aquest any.
